appDescription.message: Open-source password manager, compatible with Vaultwarden / the Bitwarden API. Built to stay light.

cmdGenerate.message: Generate a password and copy it

twoFaWebAuthnOnly.message: This account offers WebAuthn only, which is not supported yet. Enable the YubiKey's OTP mode, or TOTP on the server.

listFullLog.message: Full log: right-click the popup → “Inspect” → Console.

itemShowOtp.message: One-time code — shows and copies it

editPasskeyNote.message: Passkey preserved as-is — WebAuthn signing will arrive in a future version.

cardCheckDigitFailed.message: This number fails its check digit — one digit is wrong or two are swapped.

genAvoidAmbiguous.message: Avoid ambiguous characters (l 1 I O 0 o)

repromptDetail.message: “$1” is protected by a re-entry prompt.

settingsBreachEnable.message: Check passwords against Have I Been Pwned

settingsBreachHint.message: Off by default, and the only thing in Zwarden that talks to anyone but your own server. Your password never leaves, nor does its full hash: only the first five hex characters of its SHA-1 are sent, and the server answers with the eight hundred or so suffixes beginning with them, which are compared here. It cannot tell which one you asked about. What it does see is your IP address, that you run a password manager, and when you checked — and roughly how many passwords you hold, if you check them all at once. The answer is padded so its size says nothing either. It runs only when you ask for the health report, never on its own.

healthBreachOff.message: Breach checking is off. It can be switched on in the settings — read what it sends before you do.

exportIntro.message: A copy of the whole vault, in one file, encrypted with a passphrase of your choosing. There is no unencrypted export: such a file ends up in a downloads folder, in every backup, and on the drive when it is resold.

exportMasterHint.message: Asked once, so that items set to demand it again are included. Without it the backup would be missing exactly what matters most.

exportPassphraseHint.message: Long rather than complicated. Nobody can recover it for you: lose it and the file is noise.

exportAlgorithm.message: Argon2id then AES-256-GCM. The parameters travel in clear inside the file and are authenticated with it: lowering them makes the file refuse to open, not open weaker.

healthGuarded.message: $1 item(s) were not examined: they ask for the master password again, and an aggregate would say as much as a copy.

healthEchoing.message: Passwords that repeat the site or the account

healthStale.message: Passwords unchanged for a long time

healthDisclaimer.message: A “weak” verdict is reliable; the absence of one is not a certificate. This is an estimate computed on this machine, with no dictionary and no network.

healthDeleteHint.message: Deleted items go to the trash and can be restored from the web vault for thirty days.

healthReasonNotorious.message: among the most used in the world

queueSavedOffline.message: Saved on this device — it will be sent when the server can be reached.

queueHeld.message: $1 change(s) could not be applied: the item changed elsewhere in the meantime.

queueHeldDetail.message: Nothing was overwritten. Discard them and make the change again on the current version.

proposalNoUsername.message: (username not detected — fill it in after saving)

errorServerUnreachable.message: Server unreachable — retry, or unlock again.

errorSessionExpired.message: Session expired — lock, then unlock again.

errorSessionNoRefresh.message: Session expired without a refresh token

errorItemNotFound.message: Item not found — resync, then try again.

errorTabMismatch.message: The active tab no longer matches this item.

settingsDeviceName.message: Device name (shown among the server's active sessions)

settingsLanguageHint.message: Chrome hands an extension its own language and offers no way to change it, so Zwarden loads the chosen catalogue itself. Two things stay outside its reach, because the browser reads them before any of this code runs: the extension’s name and description, and the shortcut labels on chrome://extensions. A missing translation falls back to English rather than showing a blank label.

settingsAutoLockHint.message: “Inactivity” means: no tab, window or page change, and the popup closed. Simply browsing is therefore enough to keep the vault open. Locking may run up to a minute past the chosen delay. When the browser closes, the vault is locked regardless: the key only ever lives in memory.

settingsLockOnSystemLock.message: Also lock when the computer's session locks

settingsLockOnSystemLockHint.message: Lock screen, sleep, “Win+L”: the vault locks immediately, whatever the delay above. Walking away from your machine happens more often than closing your browser.

settingsClipboard.message: Wipe the clipboard after a copy

settingsClipboardHint.message: Two wipes back this up: a timer that honours the exact delay while the popup is open, and an alarm that survives its closing but that Chrome raises to thirty seconds minimum.

settingsOfferToSave.message: Offer to save credentials entered on an unknown site

settingsOfferToSaveHint.message: A detector watches sign-in forms and signals an entry with a badge on the icon; the offer appears when the popup opens. Nothing is added to the vault without a click, nothing is injected into the page, and nothing is sent anywhere but to the extension. Unticked, the detector is not injected at all — not a silent script, no script.

settingsRegenerateConfirm.message:
Regenerate the device identifier?

The server will see a new device: an extra session will appear in the list, a "new device" alert may be sent, and this device's 2FA exemptions will become invalid.

settingsTwoFaForgotten.message: $1 2FA exemption(s) forgotten — the second factor will be asked for again.

settingsExcludedRestored.message: $1 site(s) restored — saving will be offered there again.

settingsOrderingForgotten.message: Use ordering forgotten — the list returns to the server order.
